item.title: The Colonial Roots Of Captive Labour: From Prison Carpets To The Modern Gig Economy
item.description: The Colonial Roots Of Captive Labour In colonial India, prison carpets were marketed as symbols of craft and reform, while hiding forced labour. Today’s gig economy uses words like ”flexibility” and ”independence” to conceal similar power imbalances.

item.title: Wuthering Heights: India Wants Its Mughal Necklace Back, But Not the Mughals
item.description: Mughal Treasures, National Identity & The Battle Over Who Owns History Margot Robbie’s appearance in the “Taj Mahal” necklace reignites a debate as India wants to reclaim Mughal treasures as national heritage, even as it tries to erase the Mughals.

item.title: A Homegrown Guide To India Art Fair 2026
item.description: IAF2026: South Asia’s biggest Art Moment is Back From immersive installations and cutting-edge contemporary work to performance art, film programmes, and city-wide shows — here’s your curated guide to India Art Fair 2026.

item.title: Inside Jin Min Cat World, India’s First Museum Dedicated To Cats
item.description: Inside Jin Min Cat World, India’s First Museum Dedicated To Cats Home to over 20 cats across multiple breeds, Jin Min Cat World focuses on feline behaviour, their nutrition, and health.

item.description: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan & His Sons Become The Only Indian Musicians On A Grammy-Winning Project This Year The project, produced by Kabir Sehgal is a spoken-word album that focuses on the Dalai Lama’s core teachings.

item.description: Burgers, Beats, & Boxing Rings: The Monkey Business Pop-Up Takes Over Bengaluru The pop-up blends underground culture with a hands-on look at the city’s independent creative scene and the maker-driven energy of the studio itself.

item.title: 'Manual': Inside Black&Beige's Neo-Archival Exploration Of Analogue Culture
item.description: Learning to Listen Again: Manual’s Neo-Archival Love Letter To Analog Culture In an age of endless scrolls, Manual asks us to slow down, listen intentionally, and rediscover the quiet rituals that once shaped how we consumed culture.

item.title: Inside The Aranyani Pavilion: Tara Lal’s Vision For A Decolonised & Ecological Future
item.description: A Sacred Grove For The City Delhi’s newest landmark is made of an invasive species. The Aranyani Pavilion at Sunder Nursery transforms lantana into living architecture and reimagines how we relate to land and nature.

item.title: In 'Deepfaking Sam Altman', Devi Singh Jadoun Builds An Uncanny Valley 'Sam Bot'
item.description: Adam Bhala Lough’s Documentary Deepfakes Sam Altman To Examine Our Relationship With AI Adam travels to India to team up with Devi Singh Jadoun, a deepfake artist, to build ‘Sam Bot’ — a digital simulacrum of the CEO.
